questions.q: Why do cash bonuses often make creative work worse?
a: The pressure of the reward makes people unable to perform
The reward makes tasks feel too easy to bother with
The money distracts people from their long-term careers
The bonus encourages people to take fewer creative risks
questions.why: Lesson 1 says rewards add so much pressure that workers can no longer perform creative tasks well.

questions.q: What happened to children who were rewarded for drawing?
a: They later refused to draw unless they got a reward
They drew more often but with less original ideas
They asked for bigger rewards each time they drew
They stopped drawing and took up other hobbies
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes an experiment where rewarded children later refused to draw without the incentive, while the others kept drawing for fun.

questions.q: What three things does Pink say workers need for motivation 3.0?
a: Freedom to direct their work, a sense of purpose and room to improve
Bonuses, promotions and public recognition
Clear targets, tight deadlines and close supervision
Job security, flexible hours and generous benefits
questions.why: The overview says Pink wants workers to have control, a clear purpose and room to get better at their craft.

questions.q: What did the mechanic promised a bonus for 200 repairs do?
a: He told more customers their cars needed unnecessary repairs
He refused the bonus because the target felt unfair
He slowed down so the work would last three months
He handed some repairs to colleagues to share the reward
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the mechanic to show how a quota bonus leads to needless repairs and sloppy work rather than better, faster service.

questions.q: When does work feel like the flow state described in the summary?
a: When a task stretches your skills and you do it autonomously
When a task is easy enough to finish without thinking
When a manager sets a clear deadline and checks in often
When a bonus is large enough to justify the effort
questions.why: Lesson 3 says flow comes from a task that challenges your skills without overwhelming or boring you, done with autonomy.
